text: Which melanocyte-specific genes (single-cell) have no detectable mRNA in liver and none in kidney?
plan: Cell type category (scRNA): Melanocytes / Cell type enriched AND Tissue category (RNA): Liver / Not detected AND Tissue category (RNA): Kidney / Not detected
understanding: Identify genes that are specifically expressed in melanocytes based on single-cell RNA sequencing data, and have no detectable RNA expression in liver and kidney tissues.

trail.why: The requirement asks for melanocyte-specific genes in single-cell data, which corresponds to selecting 'Melanocytes' at level 1 and the specificity category 'Cell type enriched' (defined as at least four-fold higher mRNA compared to any other cell type) at level 2.
The requirement asks for no detectable mRNA in liver, which corresponds to selecting 'liver' at Level 1 and 'Not detected' (mRNA below the detection cut-off of 1 nTPM) at Level 2.
The requirement specifies no detectable mRNA in kidney, which corresponds to selecting 'kidney' at level 1 and 'Not detected' at level 2.

requirements.why: It defines RNA specificity categories across single cell types, including Melanocytes, whereas Cell type enrichment (RNA) covers enrichment within a given tissue rather than global single-cell specificity categories.
It evaluates tissue-level RNA expression categories (including not detected) across human tissues including liver.
It evaluates tissue-level RNA expression categories across human tissues including kidney.
